slides.title: Working with JSON
slides.html:
JSON

Working with JSON

  • JSON is text that looks like a JS object
  • Keys and strings use double quotes
  • JSON.parse: text → object
  • JSON.stringify: object → text

json.js

const text = '{"name":"Ada","skills":["HTML","CSS"]}';
 
const user = JSON.parse(text);
console.log(user.skills[1]);   // "CSS"
 
const back = JSON.stringify(user);
// '{"name":"Ada","skills":["HTML","CSS"]}'
 
const pretty = JSON.stringify(user, null, 2);

slides.title: Promises and async/await
slides.html:
Async

Promises and async/await

  • Network requests take time
  • A Promise is a value that arrives later
  • await waits for it inside an async function
  • try/catch handles failures

async.js

async function getUser() {
  try {
    const res = await fetch("/api/users/1");
    const user = await res.json();
    console.log(user.name);
  } catch (error) {
    console.log("Something went wrong", error);
  }
}
 
// same thing with .then()
fetch("/api/users/1").then((r) => r.json()).then(console.log);

slides.title: Making requests with fetch
slides.html:
Fetch

Making requests with fetch

  • GET is the default
  • For POST: method, headers and a JSON body
  • Check res.ok: fetch doesn't throw on 404 or 500

api.js

const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/tasks", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ title: "Learn fetch" }),
});
 
if (!res.ok) {
  throw new Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`);
}
 
const task = await res.json();

slides.title: Loading and error states
slides.html:
React

Loading and error states

  • Every request has 3 states: loading, error, done
  • Show a spinner, a friendly error, or the data
  • Give users a way to try again

useData.jsx

const [data, setData] = useState([]);
const [status, setStatus] = useState("loading");
 
const load = async () => {
  setStatus("loading");
  try {
    const res = await fetch(URL);
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error();
    setData(await res.json());
    setStatus("done");
  } catch {
    setStatus("error");
  }
};

slides.title: Git is a save button with a time machine.
slides.html:
Git

Git is a save button with a time machine.

Every commit is a snapshot of your project you can return to. GitHub keeps those snapshots online so you can share them and work with others.

slides.title: Git basics: init, add, commit
slides.html:
Git

Git basics: init, add, commit

  • init: start tracking a folder (once)
  • add: choose what goes in the next snapshot
  • commit: save the snapshot with a message
  • status and log show what's going on

Terminal

git init                      # start tracking
git status                    # what changed?
git add .                     # stage everything
git commit -m "Add job list"  # save a snapshot
git log --oneline             # history
 
# write clear messages:
# "Add search to job list" ✅
# "stuff" ❌

slides.title: Branches and merging
slides.html:
Git

Branches and merging

  • A branch is a safe copy to try something
  • main stays working while you build
  • Merge the branch back when it's ready
  • Conflicts happen when two changes touch the same line

Terminal

git switch -c add-search    # new branch
# ...edit files...
git add .
git commit -m "Add search box"
 
git switch main             # back to main
git merge add-search        # bring changes in
git branch -d add-search    # tidy up

slides.title: Push, pull and clone
slides.html:
GitHub

Push, pull and clone

  • push: send your commits to GitHub
  • pull: get the latest from GitHub
  • clone: download a repo to your laptop
  • Always pull before you start work

Terminal

# connect a local project (once)
git remote add origin https://github.com/you/app.git
git push -u origin main
 
git push                    # upload new commits
git pull                    # download others' commits
 
git clone https://github.com/you/app.git

slides.title: Country explorer
slides.html:
Build

Country explorer

  • Fetch once when the page loads
  • Filter as the user types
  • Show loading, error and empty states

App.jsx

const [countries, setCountries] = useState([]);
const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
const [status, setStatus] = useState("loading");
 
useEffect(() => {
  fetch("https://restcountries.com/v3.1/all?fields=name,flags,capital")
    .then((r) => r.json())
    .then((data) => { setCountries(data); setStatus("done"); })
    .catch(() => setStatus("error"));
}, []);
 
const shown = countries.filter((c) =>
  c.name.common.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())
);
